text: 🔺 **F-2299-1 — OWNER'S DESK (2026-09-24, from the rotation check after the owner's "Ok, I updaed all the keys"): the rotation's last mile: two new values into `.env.local`, and the Claude Code token still the exposed one.** VERIFIED 2026-09-24 read-only, no value printed or copied: the edge API token in `.env.local` is DEAD at its provider (the token-verify endpoint answers `1000 Invalid API Token`) and the voice key is DEAD (`HTTP 401` on the user endpoint), so both rotations happened at the providers; but `.env.local` was last written 2026-09-20, so the file `scripts/deploy.sh` sources still holds the dead values and **every deploy aborts at the wrangler auth until the owner pastes the new `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=` and `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=` lines** (a failed deploy in a fire log until then is THIS, not a regression; do not file it). The fires' own credential, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (the "coding-agent subscription token" of ruling 1), still authenticates through the fires' exact path (`claude auth status` under `~/.claude-fires` reads loggedIn; a one-word `-p` probe answered), so the value exposed on 2026-08-25 is STILL LIVE: the owner mints a new one (`claude setup-token`), pastes it as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=`, and revokes the old one in his account; the attended session re-probes and closes. The droplet holds no stray copy (`find / -name .env.local` empty, `/opt/goldrush/.env.local` absent, read-only over the deploy's own ssh path). The Codex login was refreshed today (`~/.codex/auth.json`, "Logged in using ChatGPT"). Retires when: both new values answer live to the same read-only calls, the Claude probe passes on a NEW value (`.env.local` rewritten) and the owner says the old one is revoked. The original finding is the F-2299-1 row of s2299 below. ➡️ **UPDATE 2026-09-24 18:15 local (owner: "I rotated all tokens in the .env.local file", "I rolled it again"):** the owner rotated all three at the providers and minted a new Claude Code token, but pasted twice into the sibling folder's copy (`Gold Rush-history-local/.env.local`, the pre-rewrite local history), which nothing reads; the attended session found it by mtime, verified its values read-only (Cloudflare `active`, ElevenLabs `200`, the new Claude token answers through the fires' path, per-line hashes: the three rotated lines DIFFERENT, the account id, the router key and the droplet host identical), backed the old root file up outside every git tree (`~/.goldrush/env.local.bak-2026-09-24`, mode 600; a `.bak` beside `.env.local` would NOT be gitignored) and copied the edited file into the repo root; re-verified from the root: Cloudflare `active`, ElevenLabs `200`, Claude `ok`, `wrangler whoami` logged in. DEPLOYS UNBLOCKED. STILL OPEN: the Claude Code token exposed on 2026-08-25 still authenticated at 18:14 when probed from the old file, so it is not revoked; the desk item narrows to that one revocation (the owner's account settings), verified afterwards by the same probe against the backup. ➡️ **UPDATE 2026-09-24 23:2x local (owner, verbatim: "I used the log out of all devices button in the web ui. Then I logged in again, logged in here, then did claude setup-token, copied it in .env.local and then told you done."):** MEASURED, not inferred: after that button, the August token (from the backup) and the 18:13 token (minted before the button) BOTH still answer through the fires' auth path; the button ends browser and CLI sessions (this CLI needed `/login`) but does not revoke long-lived `claude setup-token` tokens. The CLI cannot revoke either (`claude auth logout` clears local credentials only; the only revoke code in the binary is a bundled Google OAuth library; the account endpoints refuse the token with `permission_error`, so its e-mail cannot be read from the token; every login recorded on this Mac is `robin@brainstem.health`, and the fires' config dir dates from 2026-07-08, so the token was minted on or before that day). The newest token (23:16) had again gone to the sibling folder's file; copied into the repo root with the 18:15 root kept at `~/.goldrush/env.local.bak-2026-09-24-1815` (mode 600); root re-verified: Claude ok, Cloudflare active, ElevenLabs 200. REMAINING, owner-side: an Anthropic support request to revoke the Claude Code token minted on or before 2026-07-08 for `robin@brainstem.health` (the exposed one; the 2026-09-24 tokens stay), or its natural expiry; the attended session re-probes from the backup and closes the row when it fails. Exposure bound meanwhile: inference on the owner's subscription only (the account endpoints refuse it). ➡️ **SUPPORT REQUEST ISSUED (owner 2026-09-25, verbatim: "support request is issued"):** the revocation of the August Claude Code token is with Anthropic support; the attended session re-probes the backup token each session (`claude -p ok` under the fires' config from `~/.goldrush/env.local.bak-2026-09-24`) and closes this row, retires the desk item and removes both backup files (owner's word; `rm` prompts) on the first refusal. Until then: live, inference scope only. RULED 2026-09-26 (verbatim "D - as you recommend it"): the attended session keeps re-probing the backup token and retires this row, removing both backup files, on the first refusal.

🔺 **F-2296-1 OPEN — OWNER (s2296 2026-08-25): THE LIVE ASSAYER'S ENGINE IDENTITY MATCHES NO RECENT MAIN TREE, SO THE COUNTY CANNOT VERIFY ANY SUBMISSION.** Both HEAT 6 slices (`gauntlet-heat6-almanac-era` lane-c, `gauntlet-heat6-guests` lane-b) stopped at this one gate and neither could act on it — the assayer is deployed infrastructure, outside every lane firewall. Their masters bind `skew -> STOP`, and both runners obeyed rather than minting rows the assayer cannot verify: a firewall SUCCESS, not a Silent No-Op, and both wrote WHY. 📊 **MEASURED s2296, NOT INHERITED** (`computeEngineHash` from `scripts/assay-replay-agent.mjs`, 11 source inputs, run against materialised worktrees): the live advertised build `5109241a8` hashes **`d48987df2d50c643e854a2bf8a23b7f34b81c3de1cfd2e54999129b5660f7494`** — **byte-identical to the tape the rider submitted** — and main HEAD after the drain hashes the SAME, no engine input having moved since the deploy. The live assayer reports **`0be37691327931e7a3230f10fa5f65105cfc4b69af13845f84e05dfb281f3b0a`**, which reproduces from NONE of the recent main trees tested: `0cceb7d13` `587001a9…`, `0b8e8d378` `d6cebb3a…`, `22d0e1cc7` `360cdf56…`, `241ba0301` `32c798bb…`. 🔑 **THEREFORE THE TAPE IS HONEST AND THE ASSAYER IS THE DIVERGENT SIDE** — the rider really did ride the build the county advertises — and the assayer is not merely one merge behind; it is on a tree not identified. ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND NOT INFLATED: the DIRECTION IS CONSERVATIVE.** The assayer REFUSES rather than ranking what it cannot reproduce, so nothing false has entered the standings and no player was credited wrongly. What earns a blocking finding is that the refusal is total and invisible to a rider until AFTER the ride: every submission from the advertised build is unassayable, which stops the gauntlet program, the Baron admission evidence, and the announcement-week standings the desk is waiting on. 🚫 **NOT CURED BY THIS FIRE, DELIBERATELY: the fix is a DEPLOYMENT act on the droplet and §7.3 routes external-service and deployment decisions to the OWNER.** ⚠️ **AND THE CURE IS NOT "RE-PIN THE EXPECTED HASH" — the skew check is doing its job, and re-pinning would make the instrument agree with a tree nobody has identified (the re-pin reflex F-1441-3 forbids). IDENTIFY THE ASSAYER'S TREE FIRST.** **One word: (a) re-deploy the assay worker from today's main and re-run the HEAT 6 probe · (b) first identify the assayer's tree (it may hold local edits worth reading before they are overwritten), then re-deploy · (c) leave it and ship the announcement without verified standings. Recommendation (b)** — a hash matching no known commit is itself evidence, and overwriting it destroys the only copy. Evidence: `reviews/gauntlet-heat6-almanac-era.md`, `reviews/gauntlet-heat6-guests.md`, `artifacts/gauntlet-heat6-20260825/probe/verdict-slip.json`, `artifacts/gauntlet-heat6-guests-20260825/probe/verdict-slip.json`. ⛔ **PREMISE REFUTED s2297 (F-2297-1) — THE ASSAYER'S TREE IS IDENTIFIED, AND RECOMMENDATION (b) HAS LOST ITS REASON. The row above is RESTATED, NOT DELETED: its method was sound and its five-tree sample honest — the answer simply sat ~4.5 h further back than the trees it reached.** 📊 **MEASURED s2297 over EVERY commit on EVERY ref since 2026-08-21** (the engine-hash concept begins 2026-08-22, so earlier trees are UNHASHABLE by construction), **control asserted first (F-2215-1): a git-tree reimplementation of `computeEngineHash` reproduces the REAL function byte-exactly at HEAD (`d48987df…`, 481 files) before any negative was believed.** The assayer's `0be37691…` **reproduces EXACTLY, from 12 commits — `9958fefbc` (03:51:05) through `e48c2fdf8` (06:29:55) on 2026-08-25 — and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms ALL TWELVE ARE ANCESTORS OF MAIN.** 🔑 **So the assayer is NOT on an unidentified tree and holds NO local edits: it is a plain main tree, roughly 4.5 h stale at submission time. Nothing forensic is destroyed by re-deploying, because there is nothing on that box that is not already in git — which is precisely the reasoning (b) rested on. ➡️ RE-PRICED RECOMMENDATION: (a) is now the safe cheap unblock for TODAY, but see F-2297-1 — it will break again on the next guard leg, so (a) alone buys hours, not a fix.** ⚖️ **UNDISTURBED: the direction is still CONSERVATIVE, the tape is still honest, the assayer is still the divergent side, and nothing false has entered the standings.** Evidence: `artifacts/f2297-1-engine-identity-churn/note.md`.

🔺 **F-2298-1 OPEN — OWNER (s2298 2026-08-25): THE FRESHLY-LANDED ASSAYER DEPLOY LEG PUSHES 7.73 GB AND A LIVE API TOKEN TO THE DROPLET.** Measured READ-ONLY on a dry board five minutes after `3ff1eb606` landed the F-2297-1(b) cure — the leg is ONE COMMIT OLD, has never executed, and DEPLOY LAW fires it automatically on the next gameplay-affecting merge (two heat-6 r2 runs were live on lanes b/c as this was written, so its first run is imminent). 📐 **THE DIVERGENCE: `docs/ops/agenttown-server.md:40` prescribes an ALLOWLIST of nine lean paths; the leg ships a DENYLIST — `rsync -az --delete ./` minus nine names — and `deploy.sh:6–7` cds to the repo root, with the only other `cd` (`:65`) inside a subshell, so `./` IS the whole repo (verified by reading).** 📊 **MEASURED: 165 top-level entries sent, 155 outside the runbook allowlist, `7,729.9 MB` of extra payload — `e1-review-video` 3,281.6 MB and `gate-s1662` 1,576.6 MB are GITIGNORED LOCAL DEBRIS (4.86 GB that exists only on Robin's disk), plus `reviews` 1,449.8 MB, `env` 656.3 MB, `marketing` 378.5 MB incl. unpublished outbox drafts.** 🔑 **AND THE SECRET: `.env.local` (428 B, mode 600, gitignored, untracked) is NOT excluded and `rsync -a` sends dotfiles, so a live Cloudflare token lands at `/opt/goldrush/.env.local` — the file the runbook (`:42`) says is "never committed", contradicting the l4 design principle recorded in the LB-01 duty, "no new secrets on the box". The box does not need it: both services read `/etc/goldrush-*`, outside the synced tree, which is where the leg's own `sed -i` writes.** ⚖️ **SEVERITY NOT INFLATED, AND TWO SCARIER READINGS ARE REFUTED: the county LEDGER IS SAFE — it lives at `/opt/goldrush-ledger/` (`ledger-backup-pull.mjs:7`, runbook `:100`–`:108`), a SIBLING of the synced dir, so no rsync under `/opt/goldrush/` can reach it; and `node_modules` IS SAFE — rsync protects excluded names from `--delete` by default. The leg also gets one thing RIGHT that any rewrite must keep: `server/` (what `goldrush-ledger.service` RUNS, runbook `:60`) is MISSING from the runbook's own allowlist and the denylist syncs it. Fail-open is correctly built — all three arms declare which path they took.** ❓ **NOT VERIFIED AND UNCLOSEABLE FROM THIS DISK: the box's actual tree was not enumerated (that needs ssh to production, which a fire has no authorization for), so the full `--delete` blast radius over hand-placed files remains UNKNOWN.** 🚫 **NO CURE AUTHORED, FOR THREE REASONS: §7.3 routes any deployment act to the OWNER (F-2297-1's own restraint note says so, and this leg IS its option (b)); attended landed it five minutes before this fire and may still be iterating (Mistake #6); and THE OBVIOUS CURE IS SUBTLY WRONG — switching to the runbook allowlist while keeping `--delete` would DELETE `/opt/goldrush/node_modules` on a git-less box, since with an explicit source list it is neither in the source nor exclude-protected. A fire that "fixed" this in passing would break the assayer the attended session just built to unblock launch week.** ➡️ **ONE WORD: (a) minimum — add `--exclude .env.local`, strictly subtractive, removes the secret, cannot break the sync · (b) full — the runbook allowlist PLUS `server/`, retaining `--exclude node_modules --exclude dist --exclude .git` so `--delete` cannot strip the box · (c) leave it and sync by hand per the runbook. Recommendation (a) TODAY then (b)** — (a) is safe under any reading and takes one line; (b) ends the 7.7 GB and the denylist rot. ⓘ Also worth a word: the second `ssh` (`sed`+`systemctl restart`) has `BatchMode` but NO `ConnectTimeout`, where the probe ssh has `ConnectTimeout=8` — a box that accepts TCP then stalls hangs the deploy unbounded inside a fire's budget. Evidence: `artifacts/f2298-1-deploy-sync-payload/note.md` (reproduce recipe in §8). ✅ **OPTION (a) EXECUTED s2299 at `909d8c4ae` — and TWO OF THIS ROW'S FACTS ARE CORRECTED BY THE EXECUTION, both in the direction of MORE severity, so re-read F-2299-1 before ruling on (b)/(c).** (1) The payload is **FIVE live credentials, not "a live Cloudflare token"** — `.env.local` carries `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and **`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`**, the factory's own Claude subscription credential. (2) **The leg is NOT a divergence from the runbook** — it is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the runbook's own denylist recipe at `:57`, which contradicts the allowlist at `:40`; so the leak predates the leg and lives in the DOCUMENTED HAND RECIPE, widening the exposure window from "since 12:21 today" to UNKNOWN. **(b) and (c) remain fully OPEN and untouched — the 7.73 GB payload question is not answered by this fix, and s2298's warning that an allowlist plus `--delete` would strip `/opt/goldrush/node_modules` was re-verified and still holds.** The `ConnectTimeout` note also remains open.

🔺 **F-2299-1 OPEN, NARROWED 2026-09-24 to the Claude Code token and two local pastes (the desk row at the top) — OWNER (s2299 2026-08-25): THE DROPLET SYNC SHIPPED FIVE LIVE CREDENTIALS, AND THE LEAK WAS IN THE RUNBOOK'S OWN RECIPE, NOT THE NEW LEG — CURED ONE LINE, BUT A COPY MAY ALREADY BE ON THE BOX.** Executing F-2298-1's recommendation (a) on a dry board. **Measured LOCAL and READ-ONLY: no ssh to production, nothing deployed, no credential VALUE read, printed or committed.** 🔑 **CORRECTION 1 — THE PAYLOAD IS FIVE CREDENTIALS, NOT ONE.** `.env.local` (428 B, mode 600, untracked, `.gitignore:3`) carries `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and **`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` — the factory's own Claude subscription credential, i.e. the thing that pays for every fire and every lane runner.** F-2298-1 priced this as "a live Cloudflare token"; the desk was under-informed by four keys. 🔑 **CORRECTION 2, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT MOVES THE DECISION — THE LEG IS NOT A DIVERGENCE FROM THE RUNBOOK.** F-2298-1 read `docs/ops/agenttown-server.md:40`'s allowlist and called the denylist a divergence. **The runbook contains BOTH recipes: an allowlist at `:40` and, at `:57`, a denylist that is BYTE-IDENTICAL to `deploy.sh:170` after normalising whitespace and `--timeout=60`** (verified by extracting both strings from their files and comparing, not by eye). ➡️ **So the exposure is NOT a defect the new leg introduced — it is a defect in the DOCUMENTED HAND RECIPE, which predates the leg and which the owner may have run at any time since the box was set up. The exposure window is therefore not "since 12:21 today"; it is UNKNOWN.** That is why the cure had to land in BOTH files (fix the CLASS, not the instance). ✅ **PROVEN SENT, THEN PROVEN FIXED, BY MEASUREMENT AND NOT BY READING THE EXCLUDE LIST:** a local `rsync --dry-run` reproducing the leg's exact exclude set — **read out of `deploy.sh` at run time rather than retyped, so the probe cannot drift from its subject** — lists `.env.local` in the transfer set pre-cure and not post-cure; **55,661 → 55,660 files, EXACTLY ONE REMOVED**, which is the whole evidence for "strictly subtractive". ⓘ **The probe asserted its own validity first (F-2215-1) and this was not decorative: its first run returned `0 lines` and REFUSED rather than reporting a clean result, because `rsync -n` prints nothing without an itemiser. A probe whose failure mode is an empty list is indistinguishable from good news.** 🛠️ **CURE: `--exclude .env.local` in `scripts/deploy.sh:170` AND in the runbook's `:57` recipe (`909d8c4ae`). Provably safe: nothing box-side reads that file — `goldrush-assay.service` takes `/etc/goldrush-assay.env` (runbook `:32`), `goldrush-ledger.service` uses `EnvironmentFile=/etc/goldrush-ledger.env` (`:60`), both OUTSIDE the synced tree, which is exactly where the leg's own `sed -i` writes; and `grep -rn "env.local" server/ scripts/assay-worker* scripts/ledger*` returns ZERO hits.** `bash -n scripts/deploy.sh` parses clean. ⚖️ **WHY A FIRE ACTED WHERE s2298 CORRECTLY DID NOT, STATED PLAINLY SO THE OWNER CAN VETO IT: s2298's three reasons were re-measured rather than inherited, and two no longer hold.** Its reason (3) — *"the obvious cure is subtly wrong"* — is about the ALLOWLIST rewrite and **explicitly does not apply to (a)**; its reason (2), *"attended may still be iterating"*, is refuted by measurement (`deploy.sh` unchanged since `3ff1eb606`, clean vs HEAD, 30 min quiet). Only §7.3 remained, and **this is not a deployment act** — it is a one-line subtractive edit to a pipeline script, reversible, inside CLAUDE.md §2's directly-implementable set, taken under §7.4 (owner absent + reversible) with this veto line. **It forecloses nothing: (b) and (c) stay fully open.** 🚨 **WHAT THE CURE DOES NOT DO, AND IT BOUNDS THE OWNER'S REMAINING WORK: rsync PROTECTS excluded names from `--delete` — the same property s2298 used to refute the `node_modules` scare — so if any earlier run of the runbook's `:57` recipe already placed `.env.local` on the box, THIS FIX WILL NOT REMOVE IT.** ❓ **UNCLOSEABLE FROM THIS DISK: whether a copy is already there needs ssh to production, which a fire has no authorization for.** **One word, and the first half is a two-minute check: (a) `ssh root@<droplet> 'ls -la /opt/goldrush/.env.local'` — if it exists, `rm` it AND ROTATE ALL FIVE CREDENTIALS, because a token that has sat on a public-IP box is disclosed whether or not anyone read it · (b) treat the box as clean on the grounds that the leg never ran and the hand recipe was never used · (c) rotate regardless, as cheap insurance. Recommendation (a) — it is one command and it converts an UNKNOWN into a fact.** ⓘ **Do NOT read this row as closing F-2298-1: the 7.73 GB payload, the allowlist fork, and the missing `ConnectTimeout` on the second `ssh` are all still open there.** Evidence: `artifacts/f2299-1-env-local-exposure/note.md` (reproduce recipe §5, ~10 s, local, no network).

🔺 **F-2329-1 OPEN — OWNER (s2329 2026-08-26): A VERIFIED, LIVE DEPLOY IS RECORDED AS `interrupted` IN THE ONLY MACHINE-READABLE CHANNEL, AND THE ASSAYER LEG DIED SILENTLY INSIDE IT — SO THE ENGINE/ASSAYER SKEW F-2296-1 NAMES MAY BE LIVE RIGHT NOW.** Measured LOCAL and READ-ONLY on a dry board: no ssh to production, nothing deployed, no credential value read. 📊 **THE TWO CHANNELS DISAGREE, AND ONLY ONE IS MACHINE-READABLE.** `logs/deploy.log` records `08:40:24 DEPLOYED ok https://655390f8.gold-rush-3in.pages.dev`, then `08:40:26 VERIFY attempt 1/7: … says ccedf620`, then `08:40:26 VERIFIED published ccedf620 at https://gold-rush-3in.pages.dev` — that is s2327’s handoff commit `ccedf6200`, live and confirmed against the production alias. `logs/deploy-result.json` records `{"outcome":"interrupted","url":"","publishedBuild":"ccedf620","commit":"ccedf6200…","ts":"2026-08-26T01:43:06Z"}`. ⏱️ **The timestamps are in DIFFERENT ZONES and both are correct, which is why this is easy to misread: the result file writes true UTC (`date -u`, `deploy.sh:19`) while the log writes local (`date '+%F %T'`, `:14`), so `01:43:06Z` IS `08:43:06+07` — i.e. the `interrupted` verdict was written 2m40s AFTER the deploy was verified live.** 🕳️ **THE RUN DIED INSIDE THE ASSAYER LEG, PROVEN BY ABSENCE: the log ENDS at the VERIFIED line, and NONE of the leg’s three declarations appear — `ASSAYER SYNCED` (`deploy.sh:177`), `ASSAYER SYNC FAILED mid-step` (`:179`), `ASSAYER NOT SYNCED (box unreachable)` (`:182`).** The leg is entered at `:174` and the success path exits at `finish deployed 0` (`:184`), so the process was killed between those two lines; the traps at `:43`–`:45` (`HUP`/`INT`/`TERM` → `finish interrupted`) are what wrote a result file at all, and they emit no `note`, so the log gets nothing. ✅ **SAME-DAY INTERNAL CONTROL, SAME BOX, SAME LEG, 100 MINUTES EARLIER — so this is a divergence from a proven baseline, not an untested path: `07:00:14 DEPLOYED ok` → `07:00:15 VERIFIED published d4458867` → `07:00:31 ASSAYER SYNCED: droplet tree + pin d4458867, services restarted`. The leg completed in SIXTEEN SECONDS and the box was reachable that morning.** ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED — THE PLAYER-FACING DEPLOY SUCCEEDED. `ccedf620` is verified live at the production alias; NOTHING IS BROKEN FOR THE PLAYER and this row must not be read as a failed deploy.** What is wrong is the RECORD and the ASSAYER half. (1) **The record: `outcome:"interrupted"` is TRUE about the script’s exit and FALSE about the deploy’s outcome, and the file is structurally unable to tell the two apart** — "interrupted BEFORE publishing" and "interrupted AFTER a verified publish" write the IDENTICAL `outcome`, both with `url:""`; the distinction survives only in the human-readable log, which no tool reads. (2) **The assayer: the last CONFIRMED pin is `d4458867` (07:00) while Pages now serves `ccedf620`.** If the 08:40 rsync did not complete, the droplet is pinned one build behind the live engine — which is EXACTLY the condition F-HEAT6-SKEW built this leg to prevent (the comment at `:165`–`:168`: *"a deploy that moves the game engine but not the assayer’s tree makes every fresh tape honestly unassayable"*) and re-creates the state 🔺 **F-2296-1** is already open about. ⚠️ **And `:175`’s rsync carries `--delete`, so an interrupted sync can leave a MIXED tree — the state `:179`’s message exists to warn about, and that warning never printed. "Fail-open by design" degraded to FAIL-SILENT, which is worse than a red because nothing says so.** ❓ **NOT VERIFIED AND UNCLOSEABLE FROM THIS DISK: the droplet’s actual tree and pin were not enumerated — that needs ssh to production, which a fire has no authorization for (F-2299-1’s same boundary).** 🔎 **ATTRIBUTION IS INFERRED, NOT VERIFIED, AND IS MARKED SO DELIBERATELY: rsync at `:175` carries `--timeout=60`, so a pure rsync stall should have returned inside 60 s, and the elapsed ≥2m40s is more consistent with `:176`’s ssh — which has `BatchMode=yes` but NO `ConnectTimeout`, where the `:174` probe has `ConnectTimeout=8`. That is precisely the unbounded hang F-2298-1’s closing note PREDICTED (*"a box that accepts TCP then stalls hangs the deploy unbounded inside a fire’s budget"*) — a banked prediction that has now been observed. But which step hung cannot be proven from this disk.** 🚫 **NO CURE AUTHORED, FOR THREE REASONS, EACH MEASURED RATHER THAN INHERITED.** (1) §7.3 routes deployment acts to the OWNER, and `scripts/deploy.sh` already carries two open desk items (F-2298-1 (b)/(c), F-2299-1 (a)/(b)/(c)). (2) **The obvious observability cure — carry the verified state into the result JSON — REDS A GATE: `scripts/test-deploy-contract.sh:86` asserts the EXACT field set `commit,outcome,publishedBuild,ts,url` and throws `unexpected result fields` on ANY addition.** That is a CONTRACT, not a mirror (read it before touching it), so the cure is a two-file change to a gated contract plus a new case for the trap path — which today has NONE — and not a drive-by. (3) **The obvious hang cure — add `-o ConnectTimeout=8` to `:176` — is INCOMPLETE for the observed failure: `ConnectTimeout` bounds only the TCP/handshake phase, so a box that accepts the connection and then stalls during `sed`/`systemctl restart` is still unbounded.** Shipping it would let the next fire believe the hang is bounded when it is not — the "obvious cure is subtly wrong" shape s2298 refused on, for the same reason. ➡️ **ONE WORD: (a) re-run the assayer sync by hand per the runbook and confirm the pin — it converts the UNKNOWN into a fact and closes the skew risk, the same shape as F-2299-1’s (a) · (b) bound the second ssh PROPERLY — `ConnectTimeout` PLUS `ServerAliveInterval`/`ServerAliveCountMax`, or wrap the leg in `timeout` — so a stalled box DECLARES instead of hanging; this is the real cure and changes deploy behaviour, so it needs a word · (c) let the result file say "published and verified, then interrupted", updating `test-deploy-contract.sh:86`’s exact-shape assertion in the same commit. **Recommendation (a) NOW, then (b); (c) whenever that contract is next opened.**` 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is this streak’s own lesson landing outside the instrument family that produced it: every discriminator built since F-2204-1 hunts a corpus that goes silently EMPTY. This channel does not go empty — it goes CONFIDENTLY WRONG, in a field whose value (`interrupted`) is a real, legitimate member of its own vocabulary.
